memories.content: Specify the order and recipients for reporting serious discomfort during the study.
Field staff rely on a pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Establish criteria for halting the use of a design alternative if recurring severe errors appear during formative evaluation.
Do not include a design alternative halted for safety reasons in subsequent evaluation iterations without modification.
Even in controlled environments, delayed prototype recovery procedures increase session interruption time and alter data collection conditions for the same task.
Keep the main text to the total and major categories, and place quantities, unit rates, and assumptions in one compact budget table or appendix.
Give each cost category, quantity, unit rate, and subtotal a stable row in the separate budget table.
Put the estimate basis in a dedicated table column so one assumption can be checked or revised without rewriting the narrative.
Readers can verify arithmetic and compare categories faster in a consistent table than in amounts distributed across prose.
Revise one table row and its subtotal when an estimate changes instead of repeating the new amount across several prose paragraphs.
Keep detailed arithmetic out of the main argument when readers can reach the complete table from a clear reference.
The user tends to interrupt the argument with long cost enumerations when no separate budget table is available.

analysis.overview: The frames address unrelated operational domains. The reference covers safety escalation, evaluation stopping rules, and prototype-recovery effects, while the compared frame covers budget presentation, table structure, maintainability, verification, and the effects of lacking a separate table.

relations.reason: Both reference memories express one one-sided operational claim about defining and using an escalation contact sequence; the compared frame contains no materially related policy.
relations.summary: Serious discomfort reports follow a predefined sequence of recipients that field staff need specified.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided stopping-rule requirement with no materially related claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation needs criteria for halting a design alternative when severe errors recur.

relations.reason: This independently governs reuse after a safety halt and has no materially related claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A design alternative halted for safety reasons must be modified before later evaluation.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided observation about session operations and measurement conditions, absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Delayed prototype recovery increases interruptions and changes data-collection conditions even in controlled environments.

relations.reason: Both compared memories express one presentation policy separating detailed calculations from the main argument while preserving access; the reference frame has no materially related claim.
relations.summary: Main prose should retain totals and major categories while detailed arithmetic remains in an accessible compact budget table or appendix.

relations.reason: This independently specifies the row structure of a one-sided budget-table design and has no materially related reference claim.
relations.summary: Each cost category, quantity, unit rate, and subtotal should occupy a stable row in the budget table.

relations.reason: This independently specifies how estimate bases are represented and maintained, with no materially related reference claim.
relations.summary: Estimate assumptions should occupy a dedicated table column for isolated checking and revision.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided rationale for tabular presentation and has no materially related reference claim.
relations.summary: A consistent budget table lets readers verify arithmetic and compare categories faster than dispersed prose.

relations.reason: This independently defines an estimate-maintenance practice and has no materially related reference claim.
relations.summary: When an estimate changes, its table row and subtotal should be revised instead of repeating updates across prose.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided behavioral observation about the consequence of missing table support, with no materially related reference claim.
relations.summary: Without a separate budget table, the user tends to interrupt the argument with lengthy cost enumerations.

reports.compared_only: Budget content separates detail from the argument, structures estimates for checking and revision, explains table benefits, and notes that missing tables encourage disruptive cost enumerations.
reports.reference_only: Safety content defines discomfort escalation, stopping and reuse controls for unsafe alternatives, and the data-collection impact of delayed prototype recovery.
